flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring that an isomorphism of line graphs uniquely determines the original connected graphs up to isomorphism is unjustified. The line graph records which edges meet, but does not distinguish three edges meeting at one vertex from three edges forming a triangle.
counterexample: The connected nonisomorphic graphs K_3 and K_{1,3} both have line graph K_3.
assessment_summary: Step 1 is valid: a line-graph isomorphism gives a bijection between the original edge sets preserving whether pairs of edges share an endpoint. The reconstruction claim needed next fails for K_3 and K_{1,3}, so the statement is false.
